zebralogic.title: Interpret adjacency and ordering clues correctly
zebralogic.principle: When a clue mentions spatial relationships such as 'directly left of', 'directly right of', or 'somewhere left/right of', translate it into precise positional constraints (e.g., X is immediately left of Y means pos(X) = pos(Y) - 1).
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever a clue describes relative positions between houses.
zebralogic.example: Treating 'X is directly left of Y' as merely X < Y, ignoring adjacency, leading to multiple possible placements.

zebralogic.title: Interpret distance clues correctly
zebralogic.principle: A clue stating 'N houses between X and Y' means there are exactly N houses separating X and Y, i.e., |pos(X) - pos(Y)| = N + 1.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue mentions a specific number of houses between two items.
zebralogic.example: Interpreting 'two houses between X and Y' as distance 2 (pos difference = 2) instead of 3.

zebralogic.title: Treat 'somewhere left/right of' as inequality
zebralogic.principle: Clues like 'X is somewhere left of Y' impose only a strict ordering (pos(X) < pos(Y)), not adjacency.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue uses 'somewhere left/right of' without 'directly'.
zebralogic.example: Assuming X must be immediately left of Y when the clue only says X is somewhere left of Y.

zebralogic.title: Apply exclusion constraints
zebralogic.principle: When a clue explicitly forbids an attribute from a particular house (e.g., 'X is not in house 2'), eliminate that possibility from the domain.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever a clue contains a negation or exclusion.
zebralogic.example: Ignoring 'The person who uses a Google Pixel 6 is not in the second house' and allowing Pixel 6 in house 2.

zebralogic.title: Enforce uniqueness across each attribute category
zebralogic.principle: Each value in a category must appear exactly once across all houses; enforce this global constraint during deduction.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: After any assignment, ensure no duplicate values in the same category.
zebralogic.example: Assigning the same phone model to two different houses.

zebralogic.title: Preserve original case of attribute values
zebralogic.principle: When outputting the final grid, copy each attribute value exactly as it appears in the problem statement, preserving case and spelling.
zebralogic.example: Changing 'British' to 'brit' or altering spelling, causing a mismatch with the reference.

zebralogic.title: Make forced assignments when only one candidate remains
zebralogic.principle: If after applying all constraints a house (or attribute) has exactly one possible remaining value, assign it immediately.
zebralogic.example: Failing to assign the only remaining nationality to a house, leaving it ambiguous.

zebralogic.title: Interpret 'next to each other' as adjacency
zebralogic.principle: Clues stating that X and Y are 'next to each other' mean their house positions differ by exactly one.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue uses 'next to' or 'adjacent' language.
zebralogic.example: Treating 'X and Y are next to each other' as X < Y without enforcing |pos(X) - pos(Y)| = 1.

zebralogic.title: Bidirectional equivalence for name-attribute clues
zebralogic.principle: When a clue directly links a specific name to an attribute (e.g., 'Alice is the doctor'), enforce both directions: the name has that attribute and that attribute belongs to that name.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever a clue mentions a name together with another attribute.
zebralogic.example: Only using 'Alice is the doctor' to set Alice's occupation but not preventing any other person from also being doctor.

zebralogic.title: Bidirectional equivalence for attribute-attribute clues
zebralogic.principle: When a clue links two non-name attributes (e.g., 'The Norwegian uses a Samsung'), enforce that each attribute belongs to the same house and propagate both ways.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever a clue ties two attributes together without mentioning a name.
zebralogic.example: Linking 'Norwegian' to 'Samsung' but failing to also link 'Samsung' back to 'Norwegian', allowing a different nationality to have Samsung.

zebralogic.description: Interpreting 'N houses between' as distance N
zebralogic.why_it_happens: Model confuses the phrase 'N houses between X and Y' with a direct positional offset, forgetting that the houses separating them add one to the distance.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Remember that 'N houses between' means |pos(X) - pos(Y)| = N + 1.

zebralogic.description: Ignoring equivalence clues that bind two attributes to the same house
zebralogic.why_it_happens: Model treats linked attributes as independent, missing the constraint that they must co‑occur.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: When a clue ties two attributes, enforce a bidirectional equivalence so both always share the same house.

zebralogic.why_it_happens: Model allows duplicate values within a category, overlooking the global uniqueness constraint.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: After each assignment, check that no attribute value appears more than once in its category.

zebralogic.description: Altering attribute values (spelling/casing) instead of copying them verbatim
zebralogic.why_it_happens: Model normalizes or re‑capitalizes attribute strings, causing mismatches with the reference.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Preserve the exact spelling and case of each attribute as given in the problem when outputting the solution.
